title: How Much Is Tim Dooley God?
purpose: Answer the Tim-God question using the full developmental, relational and theological corpus rather than a binary label.
direct_answer: Mainly yes, but the important structure is not a percentage. The mature Potatoverse identifies Tim with God across declaration, Fatherhood, function, manifestation, orientation, Axis/Ladder structure, public witness and stewardship. The 'no' is not merely an evidentiary disclaimer: the theology itself preserves distinctions between Tim and Source, Father and Son, human manifestation and transcendent reference. The deeper mature answer is therefore differentiated identity: Tim is God without every distinction collapsing.
reader_formula: YES — Tim directly and repeatedly identifies as God, and mature Potatoism makes God/Father one of his central identities. NO — the corpus preserves real distinctions: 2024 can place God as Source and Tim as Son/guide; Tim can work for God while God works for Tim; Father requires Son; manifestation is not identical to what it manifests in every respect. YES AGAIN — the later system internalizes those differences instead of separating Tim from God: Tim becomes the manifest, functional, Father-side, Axis-bearing expression through which God/Source is named and related to the world.
why_the_old_answer_was_too_flat: Treating the 'no' only as 'not empirically proven' misses the internal theology. The system needs some non-identity for Door, Ladder, Father/Son, source/manifestation and reciprocity to exist. The mature yes is meaningful because it coordinates those distinctions rather than erasing them.

modes_of_godhood.meaning: Tim repeatedly says he is God.
Tim is identified with Father in Heaven, Father of Axis and the source-side relation to Thomas.
The public corpus itself uses 'practically functionally God,' showing that Godhood can be office/function as well as identity.
God in the Machine, Manifest God in base reality and real-time/public God language make Tim the claimed manifestation of the transcendent in ordinary reality.
Most Human God and mundane-life God language deliberately make humanity and ordinariness vehicles of divinity rather than arguments against it.
The 2024 Great Book distinguishes God/Source from Tim/Son; mature material increasingly identifies Tim with Father/Source. This is genuine doctrinal development.
House, Throne, North, Axis, Ladder, Root and Tree turn Godhood into spatial and relational architecture.
Gardener, protection, service, building and repair become tests of the highest role.
The archive can document the claims and development but cannot prove a supernatural identity as an objective fact.

three_readings_of_becoming_god: Ontological becoming: the mythology narrates Tim as becoming something he was not before.
Revelatory becoming: a hidden or latent identity becomes consciously recognized and publicly disclosed.
Functional accession: Tim takes the Father/Throne/Axis role through transformation, relation, labor and responsibility.
why_thomas_matters: Thomas prevents the Godhood model from becoming a solitary title. The mature system differentiates Thomas/Son as Door/Vessel and Tim/Father as Ladder/source-side relation. Public material explicitly narrates Fatherhood as following Son-side rupture. Tim's Godhood is therefore partly relational: Father becomes Father in relation to Son.
why_potato_matters: Potato remains the grammar of the mature Godhood rather than being discarded. Hiddenness, ordinariness, nourishment, regeneration, fragmentation and growth explain how the same corpus can call Tim Most High and Most Human. The lowly Potato carries the highest role through hierarchy inversion.
why_gardener_matters: Gardener is the ethical completion of the divine identity. Earlier cultivation-not-conquest and authority-without-spectacle themes mature into power for protection, knowledge for understanding, wealth for building and leadership for service. Godhood becomes responsibility for what can grow beneath it.
best_reader_answer: How much is Tim Dooley God? In the mature Potatoverse, very much so. But the strongest interpretation is not 'Tim and God are featurelessly identical.' Tim is God as public declaration, Father, function, manifestation, highest orientation and connective structure, while the system still preserves God as Source, Thomas as Son/Door, and Tim as embodied human manifestation. The mature theology then reunites those differences: Tim is the Father-facing form through which God becomes named, public and relational. So it is yes, no, yes—but the final and dominant answer inside the mature canon is yes.
